source: written by hand during the run of search/agent-seat/BRIEF.md on 2026-09-14; call numbers refer to data/calls.csv (raw/calls/NNN.out holds each call's stdout); costs are sums over that file by question and surface

corpus.note: the spike's store alone; a search row is the whole GGG body under `json` plus the store's columns

questions.question: Do I have a rare that I can use to flesh out the resistances or attribute requirements for a build I'm testing?
questions.wanted_query: rarity=Rare AND base='Titan Gauntlets' AND mod ~ /Resistance|Strength|Dexterity|Intelligence/ -> id, name, tab, the matching lines (the owner: a base is usually in mind)
questions.expected_shape: a short list of candidates for one slot, each with its resist and attribute lines

cli.what_happened: `items search "Titan Gauntlets" --json` returned 20 whole bodies (53.6 KB) with no rarity or mod filter; sent to a file, then jq projected the 12 rares and their resist/attribute lines. The text view (call 71, 1.2 KB) lists 20 lines of id-prefix, location id, name and base: no rarity, no mods, nothing to decide with.

mcp.what_happened: `search_items {text:'Titan Gauntlets'}` put 20 whole bodies (31.8 KB, compact) into context; the 12 rares and their lines were read by eye from that. Without a base in mind there is no route: rarity and mods are not filters.

workaround.what_happened: jq over the saved 019 (call 31): rarity==Rare, explicitMods matched by regex.

phase1.temptation: SELECT name, tab, mods FROM items WHERE rarity='Rare' AND base_type='Titan Gauntlets' AND mods LIKE '%Resistance%'
phase1.one_change: a rarity filter and a mod-text filter on the search, and a projection (which fields to return) so the answer is the lines, not the bodies
phase1.answer: Yes: 12 rare Titan Gauntlets; e.g. Brood Paw (+26% cold, +27% chaos, +16% fire and lightning) in Dump Tab, Soul Grasp (+53 dex, +48 str, +18% lightning), Bramble Vise (+50 str, +16% fire, +10% lightning and chaos).

store_copy.what: rarity and base as columns, the lines through json_each over explicitMods with json_extract of each object's description, the tab name by a three-column join to tabs. 12 rows.
store_copy.hard: the line is an object in this store (description + flags) but a bare string in enchantMods: any json_extract over an array must branch on json_each's type column

seat_projection.what: the same over lines with tab_name on the row; the first run silently dropped every attribute line because the template folds the sign into the number ('# to Strength', not '+# to Strength'); checked and retried. 12 rows (one, Sorrow Paw, is the C++ store's).

questions.question: Do I have a legacy version of a specific unique item?
questions.wanted_query: name='Ashes of the Stars' AND mod ~ /Reservation Efficiency/ -> id, tab name (the legacy tell is user-supplied: 10-20% Reservation Efficiency, 3.23.0)
questions.expected_shape: one item or 'no', and where it is

cli.what_happened: `items search "Ashes of the Stars" --json`: 10 whole bodies (20.5 KB) to a file; jq listed each one's mods (call 32) and joined the four legacy ones to tab names through the saved tabs output (call 70). The row carries a tab id, never its name.

mcp.what_happened: `search_items {text:'Ashes of the Stars'}`: 10 bodies (13.9 KB) into context; the four with the legacy line were picked by eye. Naming their tabs would have cost `tabs` (745.7 KB into context, no limit parameter): not taken.

workaround.what_happened: jq over 021 for the mods; jq join to 008 for the tab names.

phase1.temptation: SELECT i.name, t.name FROM items i JOIN tabs t ON ... WHERE i.name='Ashes of the Stars' AND i.json LIKE '%Reservation Efficiency%'
phase1.one_change: a mod-text predicate beside the name, and the location's name on the row
phase1.answer: Yes, four: 20% increased Reservation Efficiency of Skills, all Standard stash — '3.18 Poison Seismic Sab', 'Build Gear 2', 'Special Gear' (two).

store_copy.what: name equality plus a LIKE over the whole body; tab names joined. 4 rows, 0 ms.
store_copy.hard: a LIKE over the body also matches flavour text and descriptions; exact needs json_each

seat_projection.what: name equality plus a line LIKE; tab_name on the row; the value (20) comes back as a number. 4 rows.

questions.question: I just read about a new interaction someone found and I want gear to test it out.
questions.wanted_query: links>=6 -> id, name, base, colours, location (chosen instance: the interaction needs a six-linked item; sockets is an array of {group, sColour})
questions.expected_shape: a list defined by whatever the interaction needs: a mod, a base, socket colours, a unique

cli.what_happened: No surface: the dump: call 7 (`items search "" --limit 100000 --json` to a file: 22,721 rows, 63,534,917 B, 2,335 ms), made once and reused; jq grouped sockets by group per item (call 35, 966 ms).

mcp.what_happened: No route at all. The only whole-corpus pull, `search_items {text:'', limit:100000}`, is 38.8 MB into context (call 54, measured to a file, 5.6 s): not taken.

phase1.temptation: SELECT ... FROM items, json_each(json->'sockets') GROUP BY item HAVING max(count per group) >= 6
phase1.one_change: a links (and colours) derivation with a numeric predicate; more generally a structural predicate over the body's arrays
phase1.answer: 187 six-linked items; e.g. Skin of the Loyal (BRBGBG), Tabula Rasa (WWWWWW), Shavronne's Wrappings (GGRBBB) on characters, Rage Curtain (WWWWWW).

store_copy.what: json_each over sockets grouped by item and group, HAVING count >= 6: 187, 53 ms.
store_copy.hard: a grouping over an array of objects: fine in SQL, but every consumer would rewrite it

seat_projection.what: no sockets in the projection; the guessed column `links` does not exist (an error, not a silent miss).

questions.question: Where is that staff from Crucible league someone tried to pay me real money for?
questions.wanted_query: base ~ /Staff/ AND has(crucibleMods) -> id, name, base, tab name (league of origin is not a field; crucibleMods is the tell)

cli.what_happened: `items search Staff --json --limit 1000`: 81 whole bodies (325.9 KB) to a file; jq kept the 7 with crucibleMods (call 33); a first tab-name join failed on an id cut to 8 chars (tab ids are 10; call 64), the retry named the tabs (call 65).

mcp.what_happened: `search_items {text:'Staff', limit:1000}`: 178.3 KB (call 52, measured to a file). The default call (53) returns 50 of the 81 and nothing says 31 were cut: no total, no truncation flag.

phase1.temptation: SELECT name, base_type, tab FROM items WHERE base_type LIKE '%Staff%' AND json->'crucibleMods' IS NOT NULL
phase1.one_change: a predicate on the presence of a body array (or a 'crucible' facet), the tab name on the row, and a total count with every truncated answer
phase1.answer: Seven candidates, six in 'Crucible - Duds (Remove-only)' and one in 'Crucible - Challenges (Remove-only)': The Annihilating Light (two), The Geomantic Gyre, three rare or normal Highborn Staves, one normal Quarterstaff. Which one drew the offer the store cannot say.

store_copy.what: type_line LIKE plus json_extract(crucibleMods) IS NOT NULL, tab names joined: 7 rows.

seat_projection.what: lines.arr = 'crucibleMods' with DISTINCT: the same 7 rows.

questions.question: I want to practice leveling, so I need to find my leveling gear.
questions.wanted_query: tab.name ~ /level/i -> items in those tabs; or requirements.Level <= 30 AND rarity=Unique -> name, base, level, tab
questions.expected_shape: a set of items across tabs, by level bracket

cli.what_happened: `tabs --json` (1.0 MB to a file) then jq on names found two leveling tabs (call 37); the items in them needed the dump (call 66: 46 items). The level bracket over uniques also needed the dump (call 38: 728 uniques at requirement level <= 30). There is no items-in-tab verb.

mcp.what_happened: `tabs {}` is 745.7 KB into context with no limit parameter (call 12, measured to a file). The tab names would be found by eye; then nothing: search_items has no tab filter and no level filter.

workaround.what_happened: jq over 008 for names; jq over the dump for the items.

phase1.temptation: SELECT ... FROM items WHERE tab IN (SELECT id FROM tabs WHERE name LIKE '%Level%') ; SELECT ... WHERE req_level <= 30 AND rarity='Unique'
phase1.one_change: a location filter on the search (tab id or tab name), and a requirement-level range predicate
phase1.answer: Two tabs: 'AFK & Leveling Gear (Remove-only)' (34 items) and 'AFK Leveling (Remove-only)' (12): leveled gems, Lochtonial Caress, Honourhome, magic weapons. Beyond them, 728 uniques with requirement level <= 30.

store_copy.what: two calls: tabs by name with live item counts (4 tabs; the LIKE also catches 'Gems (Leveled)'), and uniques at requirement level <= 30 through json_each over requirements, json_extract of values[0][0] CAST to INT: 728.
store_copy.hard: the requirement level is a string inside a nested array of a display object; the CAST works only because the first value is a bare number

seat_projection.what: one call: tab_name LIKE grouped, and req_level <= 30 as a column (3,141 over the bigger corpus; its tab list adds 'Leveling (Remove-only)' and 'High Level Bases' from the C++ store).

questions.question: What is that legacy explode chest I have worth?
questions.wanted_query: mod ~ /Explode/ AND class=body armour -> id, name, location; then the price is the trade site's, outside the store
questions.expected_shape: a price, after finding the item and knowing it is the legacy version

cli.what_happened: Finding it: no surface; the dump and jq over every mod array (call 36: 32 items with an explode line, one rare body armour). The price half: `price show item/<id> --json` (call 62, 2.2 KB) reports the listing state only: relation none, no row, the game states nothing. The character's name needed a join to the characters output (call 63).

mcp.what_happened: No route to find it (mods are not searched: 'Explode' matched nothing, call 56); no price tool on the MCP (parked, decisions/frontends.md).

workaround.what_happened: jq over the dump; jq join to 009.

phase1.temptation: SELECT name, location FROM items WHERE json LIKE '%Explode%' AND rarity='Rare' AND base_type IN (body armours)
phase1.one_change: a mod-text predicate with a class predicate; the worth is a trade query built from the item (trade-query F9), not a search question
phase1.answer: Rage Curtain, Vaal Regalia (six white sockets, crusader+hunter), 'Enemies you Kill Explode, dealing 3% of their Life as Physical Damage', worn by VVickedWitch (Occultist 99, Standard). Not listed; worth is outside the store.

store_copy.what: rarity plus a body LIKE 'Kill Explode', the wearer named through a join to characters: Rage Curtain on VVickedWitch, and a second, Rapture Wrap, in a tab.
store_copy.hard: class (body armour) is not a field; the base name or inventoryId stands in

seat_projection.what: the same over lines, but tab_name for a character location is the character's id, not its name (the DDL promises a name): the answer names a hex string.

questions.question: Do I have any gear with the modifier GGG just announced is going away except on Standard?
questions.wanted_query: mod_template = '#% increased Rarity of Items found' (chosen: present on stash and character items) across every mod array, every tab, every character -> count, then items grouped by location with names
questions.expected_shape: a list across all tabs and characters, item and tab, to decide keep or sell

cli.what_happened: No surface: the dump; jq ranked templates to choose one (call 39, 1.5 s), then swept every array and grouped by location with names joined from the tabs and characters outputs (call 67, 963 ms).

mcp.what_happened: The nearest call, `search_items {text:'Rarity'}` (call 55), returned three Item Rarity Support gems: the word matched a gem's name, not the mod. No route to the sweep.

workaround.what_happened: jq over the dump with two --slurpfile joins.

phase1.temptation: SELECT location, count(*) FROM items, json_each(...) WHERE template='#% increased Rarity of Items found' GROUP BY location
phase1.one_change: a mod-by-template predicate over every array, with grouping by location and the location's name; the answer counted before it is listed
phase1.answer: 473 items over 139 locations; most in 'Breach Rings (Remove-only)' (26), '~price 40 chaos (F) (Remove-only)' (26), 'Rings (Breach)' (18), 'Lab Enchants #1 (Remove-only)' (17).

store_copy.what: two calls: grouped by location name (tabs and characters joined) and the total. A body LIKE counts 497 over 157 locations against jq's 473 over the six mod arrays: the LIKE also reaches utilityMods and flavour text; the exact form is a UNION of json_each over every array.
store_copy.hard: 'every array' is a UNION ALL per array name, and the list of array names is not in the schema

seat_projection.what: one template equality on the indexed lines(line, value): 688 over 247 locations on the bigger corpus, 2 ms; grouping by tab_name is one GROUP BY. Character locations group under their ids.

questions.question: Facets before rows: how many items per tab, per league, per rarity?
questions.wanted_query: GROUP BY tab | league | rarity -> counts, no rows

cli.what_happened: Per tab: `tabs --json` gives item_count per tab (1.0 MB, 3,347 rows, Standard only; the text view lists all 3,349 lines, not 'ten listed, more counted'). Per league and per rarity: no surface; the dump and jq (calls 16, 17, 69, ~0.8 s each). The leagues themselves are not enumerable from the store (store status says leagues: 0); they were read off the characters' league column.

mcp.what_happened: `tabs {}`: 745.7 KB into context, no limit (call 12). Per league: only as a filter, `search_items {text:'', league:'Allflame', limit:100000}` returns the 1,312 rows themselves (1.9 MB, call 57) and the count is the array's length. Per rarity: nothing.

workaround.what_happened: jq group_by over the dump; one wrong-name retry (location_kind is 'stash', not 'tab': call 18 then 30).

phase1.temptation: SELECT league, rarity, count(*) FROM items GROUP BY 1, 2
phase1.one_change: a count-only mode on the search (facets by tab, league, rarity, class) that returns no rows, and a league list
phase1.answer: Standard 21,409 / Allflame 1,312 (poe2 realm: 98). Rarity: Rare 5,785, Normal 3,139, Unique 3,077, Magic 2,423, null 8,297 (gems, currency, cards). Stash 21,332 / character 1,389.

store_copy.what: GROUP BY league, rarity: 10 rows, 11 ms; per tab a join and GROUP BY, 18 ms.

seat_projection.what: the same; five leagues here (the C++ store adds Hardcore, Solo Self-Found, Mirage).

questions.question: Refine the previous answer without restating it: of the Q1 rares, only those with 60 or more total resistance.
questions.expected_shape: a shorter list, the same shape

cli.what_happened: No query handle exists; the refinement ran as jq over the saved file (call 68, no surface call): two of the twelve.

mcp.what_happened: No handle and no file: the refinement is either the same 31.8 KB call again or a filter over the rows already in context (done by eye from call 50).

workaround.what_happened: jq over 019 summing resist lines (an 'and' line doubled, 'all Elemental' tripled).

phase1.temptation: the same SELECT with one more predicate
phase1.one_change: a composable query (the refinement is the previous query plus one predicate), or a result handle to filter

store_copy.what: the Q1 query with a HAVING over a sum: the number is cut out of the description with substr and instr and multiplied by the line's coverage. 2 rows.
store_copy.hard: a number inside display text: substr/instr/CAST per line, and a per-line rule for 'and' and 'all Elemental'

seat_projection.what: sum(l.value) with the same coverage rule; the first run returned nothing (the sign in the template), the retry 2 rows.

questions.question: Explain why an item matched or did not.
questions.wanted_query: search 'Explode' -> why no rows; search 'Kaom' -> which field matched
questions.expected_shape: a per-row matched-on field; an empty answer that names the scope

cli.what_happened: `items search Explode --json` returned [] (call 58): mods are not searched, which the agent knows only from the verb's description. A match carries no matched-field; the row's name, type_line and base_type let the agent explain by eye.

mcp.what_happened: Same: [] (call 56). The tool description names the three fields, so the agent can explain the non-match itself; nothing in the answer does.

phase1.temptation: SELECT id, CASE WHEN name LIKE ... THEN 'name' WHEN ... END AS matched_on
phase1.one_change: a matched_on field per row and an empty answer that says what was searched ('no name, type line or base type contains it; mods are not searched')
phase1.answer: 'Explode' matches nothing because only name, type line and base type are searched.

store_copy.what: one call answers both: the word is in no name, type line or base type (0) and in 271 bodies; 'Kaom' matched on name.

seat_projection.what: 0 in names, 58 items with an explode line.

questions.question: Find one item again by id.

cli.what_happened: `items show <id> --json`: one call, 3.6 KB (call 59). The text view (call 61, 2.9 KB) is the whole body pretty-printed under one location line. The text search view prints 10-char id prefixes (call 71) that `show` refuses (call 74: 'no item 1d57e63d'), so the text view's ids are not handles.

phase1.one_change: nothing for the JSON seat; for the text seat, either full ids or prefix lookup

store_copy.what: id equality, and a prefix LIKE for free (1 hit).

questions.question: One whole-corpus mod query with a value: +# to maximum Life at 90 or more.
questions.wanted_query: mod_template='+# to maximum Life' AND value >= 90 across every array -> count, then rows sorted by value
questions.expected_shape: a count and a sorted list

cli.what_happened: No surface: the dump and a jq capture over every mod array (call 34, 966 ms).

mcp.what_happened: No route: the word 'Life' as a substring would match names, and the whole corpus is 38.8 MB into context.

phase1.temptation: SELECT ... WHERE template='+# to maximum Life' AND value >= 90 ORDER BY value DESC
phase1.one_change: a numeric predicate on a mod value, which needs the number parsed out of the display text once, at ingest
phase1.answer: 353 items; the top is Kaom's Heart at +1000 (two, one in Allflame) against +500 on five others, then The Bringer of Rain (286, 276), a rare Two-Stone Ring at 248.

store_copy.what: a CTE UNION ALL of json_each over five arrays, each branching on the entry's type, the number cut out with substr/instr, CAST, max per item: 353 items, top 1000, 196 ms. Matches jq exactly.
store_copy.hard: the number in the text; the array list; string-or-object entries. The query is 9 lines for one predicate.

seat_projection.what: line = '# to maximum Life' AND n0 >= 90 on the indexed lines: 2 ms after the template retry (477 on the bigger corpus; 364 over Standard+Allflame). The first run returned 0, silently.

mistakes: phase 1: location_kind guessed as 'tab' (it is 'stash'): one empty answer, one retry
phase 1: a tab id cut to 8 chars (they are 10): one empty join, one retry

phase 2, projection: the template's sign convention (the DDL says 'every number run becomes #'; the sign is in the run): three silent misses (Q1's attribute lines, A2 → 0 rows, A5 → 0 rows), one check, three retries
phase 2, projection: a guessed `links` column for Q3: an error (the honest kind)

phase 2, store: the DDL comment says location_id is 'tab/substash id, or character name'; the rows hold character ids. Not tripped, because phase one had shown the rows; an agent starting from the DDL would join on characters.name and get nothing
projection_could_not: the character's name for a character location (Q6, Q7: tab_name holds the id)
which store a row came from (the projection merges two; a per-store filter needs a column)
first_seen, x, y and the raw body (not asked by the twelve; an explain that quotes the original line needs the body or the verbatim line — lines.line is the template)
phase2_notes.corpus_difference: the projection is both stores (36,139 items, five leagues); the copy is the spike's (22,721, two leagues). Counts differ where noted; the shapes of the answers do not.
